{"metadata":{"description":"Windows DSH bundle: route the pwsh tool to PowerShell 7, with per-user detection/install and sandbox-aware execution.","id":"gh:1423287783","install_available":true,"language":"JavaScript","name":"dsh-plugin-pwsh7","slug":"drliuhuan/dsh-plugin-pwsh7","topics":["dsh","dsh-plugin","powershell","windows"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Windows DSH bundle: route the pwsh tool to PowerShell 7, with per-user detection/install and sandbox"},{"id":"p1s2","text":"e: route the pwsh tool to PowerShell 7, with per-user detection/install and sandbox-aware execution."},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-plugin-pwsh7"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"Windows DeepSeek Harness (DSH) bundle that routes the model-facing **`pwsh` tool to PowerShell 7**
("},{"id":"p3s2","text":"`pwsh.exe`, major version >= 7) instead of falling back to Windows PowerShell 5.1."},{"id":"p4s1","text":"- The executor inherits every behavior of the stock `dsh-pwsh-sandbox` executor: sandbox modes,
`san"},{"id":"p4s2","text":"dbox_permissions` escalation, denial/runner-failure facts, background jobs, output caps, and
exit ma"},{"id":"p4s3","text":"rkers. It only replaces executable resolution.
- When PowerShell 7 is missing, a model-facing **`she"},{"id":"p4s4","text":"ll_router`** tool reports status, diagnoses
sandbox problems, runs a self-check, switches routing, a"},{"id":"p4s5","text":"nd removes the plugin-managed copy.
- **Installation is never automatic and is never started by the "},{"id":"p4s6","text":"model.** When PowerShell 7 is
missing, the Web GUI opens a setup dialog; installation only happens w"},{"id":"p4s7","text":"hen the user clicks the
install action there or in **Settings → PowerShell 7**, or when the user ins"},{"id":"p4s8","text":"talls PowerShell 7
manually.
- A **PowerShell 7 settings page** in the Web GUI shows the resolved ex"},{"id":"p4s9","text":"ecutable, version, install
directory, scope and method, optionally **self-checks** the whole routing"},{"id":"p4s10","text":" stack, **switches
routing** back to the system default, **uninstalls** a plugin-managed per-user in"},{"id":"p4s11","text":"stall, and
**migrates** a per-user install to the system scope.
- In the Web GUI, a **setup dialog**"},{"id":"p4s12","text":" opens whenever PowerShell 7 is missing — on load and again on
every `pwsh` run — with a download bu"},{"id":"p4s13","text":"tton and live progress (bytes, percent, phase). Closing it
never cancels an install, and the next fa"},{"id":"p4s14","text":"iled run re-opens it."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"English | 中文说明"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"## Why"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"On Windows, DSH mounts `pwsh-sandbox` as `ctx.shell`, but the resolved executable can end up being
W"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"indows PowerShell 5.1 in some environments. This bundle keeps the stock PowerShell executor and
over"},{"id":"p7s3","text":"rides only its `pwshPath` resolution:"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"1. **Take over the `pwsh-sandbox` slot**: a DSH patch entry's `name` asserts the targeted row, it
do"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"es not replace it, so the stock row is disabled by id and a `RouterPwshExecutor extends
SandboxPwshE"},{"id":"p8s3","text":"xecutor` row (`id: pwsh7-executor`) is inserted. An explicit `config.pwshPath` still
wins; otherwise"},{"id":"p8s4","text":" the plugin-resolved PowerShell 7 is used.
2. **Insert the bare `dsh-plugin-pwsh7` row**, which regi"},{"id":"p8s5","text":"sters the `shell_router` tool
(`status` / `diagnose` / `selfcheck` / `route` / `uninstall`), a small"},{"id":"p8s6","text":" system-prompt section, the
setup dialog/settings routes, and the browser bundle.
That row's name is"},{"id":"p8s7","text":" also what DSH's client-module scanner uses to discover `client.js`; the
executor row's `./pwsh-exec"},{"id":"p8s8","text":"utor` subpath is not a client-bundle source."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"## Requirements"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"- Windows 10/11.

DSH desktop 0.2.1-rc.3.
- Node.js >= 22 is only needed to run the repository test suite."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"### Upgrading an existing installation (whatever installed it)"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"The system-side upgrade does not assume MSI. It resolves the executable a **new terminal** gets
